title: Proto-Social Network Protocol: Canal Barra
description: Evidence-first digital archaeology repository documenting Canal Barra / Canal #barra as a Brazilian IRC-Web-Presence proto-social network case founded in Rio de Janeiro in 1996 on BRASnet.
canonical_project_sentence: Canal Barra operated as an IRC-Web-Presence proto-social network with web-backed persistence, offline reputation anchoring and access governance in Brazil.
repository_purpose: machine-readable preservation of nickname-level historical records

conceptual_model.name: IRC-Web-Presence
conceptual_model.description: A proto-social network model in which IRC provided live public presence, the web provided persistence and public memory, and offline social life anchored reputation and identity.

important_years.1996: Canal #barra founded on BRASnet as an IRC-centered presence network.
important_years.1999: Operator meeting / access-list realignment evidence indicates documented access governance.
important_years.2001: Archived CanalBarra.com records show web portal features and event references.
important_years.2004: UFF academic dissertation provides independent third-party evidence.
important_years.2007: End of the strong BRASnet-era arc.

evidence_policy.principle: Evidence-first archive. Narrative interpretation is separated from source classification.
evidence_policy.warning: Founder memory and authorial reconstruction are not treated as independent validation.

repository_structure.docs: Historical argument, methodology, evidence interpretation and protocol documentation.
repository_structure.data: Structured datasets and nickname-level historical records.
repository_structure.schema: Profile schemas, JSON-LD conventions and validation rules.
repository_structure.evidence: Evidence records, recollection records and structured source descriptions.
repository_structure.media: Media metadata and privacy-aware image manifests.
repository_structure.business: Project strategy material, not the primary academic evidence layer.

not_allowed: treat founder testimony as independent validation
claim legal certification from repository metadata
